entries.outcome: Resolved. The ghost was pasted out of existence.

entries.headline: The review every agency fears, in writing: "like an inexperienced intern rushing to meet a deadline"
entries.hook: Round-one edits deleted, AI-written clinical copy spotted, premium price invoked. Devastating.

thread.speaker: Client (a dentist)
thread.text: I took time out of my busy schedule to thoroughly review and provide detailed feedback, but it's clear that my edits were not given equal attention. In fact, my first round of edits appears to have been deleted entirely. Now I have to do twice the work—first to re-enter the same changes, and second to trust they'll actually be addressed. TBH, it feels like the edits were handled by an inexperienced intern rushing to meet a deadline rather than a professional team. That's disappointing, especially since we are paying premium for your services. Will I recommend you to my colleagues? No, not really.

thread.speaker: Client (a dentist)
thread.text: What I'm specifically referring to is the content under the Services section (dental implants, sedation, jaw surgery, etc.), which appears to have been written by ChatGPT. Many of the statements are inaccurate or reflect a lack of clinical understanding. Reading through large blocks of poorly written or misinformed content is not only frustrating—it's also a poor use of my limited time.

entries.whyItMatters: This is the thread agencies have nightmares about: lost feedback AND AI-generated clinical copy that a real doctor immediately clocked as wrong. Two separate process failures, one furious domain expert, zero places to hide. If your review workflow can lose a round of edits, it will eventually lose them for the client who notices everything.
entries.outcome: Resolved - after a very long internal meeting, presumably.

entries.whyItMatters: The single most valuable sentence an agency can say, and it only works if there's a record. "This was approved" isn't a defense without a paper trail - which is exactly what a comment thread pinned to the page is.

entries.headline: A copy note that starts with "just checking" and ends with "please google Australian spelling!"
entries.hook: "Fueling is a spelling error - it's fuelling." Weaponized politeness, gold standard.

thread.speaker: Client
thread.text: This needs a readability re-write. Suggest something like: Fuelling innovative health research. Just checking you're using Grammarly or an equivalent extension to check spelling too? Fueling is a spelling error - it's fuelling. Please ensure you're using this throughout and if you're unsure - please google Australian spelling!

entries.whyItMatters: Every word here is polite and every word is a knife. "Just checking," "please ensure," "if you're unsure" - and then the exclamation mark lands like a slammed door. Localisation isn't only translation; sometimes it's one L, and someone will absolutely notice.
entries.outcome: Open. Somewhere, a US spell-checker is still winning.

samples.headline: No llms.txt - AI assistants are guessing what your product does
samples.hook: ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity answer questions about your category. Without you.

finding.title: No llms.txt or AI-readable product summary found
finding.description: The site publishes nothing AI assistants can reliably ingest: no llms.txt, no machine-readable summary of what the product does, who it's for, or how it's priced. Assistants answering "best tools for X" fall back to third-party listicles - and cite your competitors.
finding.suggestion: Publish llms.txt covering product, audience, pricing, and FAQ pointers; keep it generated from the marketing site so it never drifts.

samples.whyItMatters: Search traffic is becoming answer traffic. AEO - being the source AI assistants cite - is the new page-one, and most sites haven't noticed they're invisible there.
samples.note: Illustrative example - the AEO agent is newly shipped, so this shows the report format rather than a customer catch.

samples.headline: robots.txt blocks the exact AI crawlers you want citing you
samples.hook: GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot: all disallowed. Assistants quote your competitors instead.

finding.title: AI crawlers disallowed sitewide in robots.txt
finding.description: robots.txt disallows GPTBot, ClaudeBot, and PerplexityBot across the whole site - including docs and pricing, the pages you most want AI assistants to cite. Assistants now answer questions about the product from third-party summaries, which are stale and sometimes wrong.
finding.suggestion: Allowlist chosen AI crawlers for /docs, /pricing, and /blog while keeping private paths blocked. Blocking everything is a decision - make it on purpose.

samples.whyItMatters: Teams copy-pasted "block all bots" robots rules in 2023 and never revisited them. Three years later, that one file decides whether AI assistants describe your product accurately, wrongly - or not at all.
samples.note: Illustrative example - the AEO agent is newly shipped, so this shows the report format rather than a customer catch.
